# Page: Topology and Metadata Generation

# Topology and Metadata Generation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [manual_tools/inputs_generator_by_pdb.py](manual_tools/inputs_generator_by_pdb.py)
- [model_workflow/resources/inputs_file_template.yml](model_workflow/resources/inputs_file_template.yml)
- [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py](model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py)
- [model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py](model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py)
- [model_workflow/tools/get_bonds.py](model_workflow/tools/get_bonds.py)
- [model_workflow/tools/image_and_fit.py](model_workflow/tools/image_and_fit.py)
- [model_workflow/tools/structure_corrector.py](model_workflow/tools/structure_corrector.py)

</details>



This page documents the topology and metadata generation components of the MDDB-workflow system. These components are responsible for creating standardized JSON representations of molecular structures and capturing comprehensive information about molecular dynamics simulations. The generated files are essential for both analysis and database storage.

For information about trajectory manipulation prior to these steps, see [Trajectory Manipulation](#3.3). For information about mapping generation that feeds into metadata, see [Mapping Generation](#3.4).

## Overview

After a molecular dynamics simulation has been processed, corrected, and mapped, the workflow generates two critical files:

1. **Topology file**: A comprehensive JSON representation of the molecular structure including atoms, bonds, residues, chains, and their properties.
2. **Metadata file**: Contains detailed information about the simulation parameters, structure statistics, and reference information required for database storage and front-end display.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Previous Steps"
        StructCorr["Structure Correction"]
        Mapping["Mapping Generation"]
        ImageFit["Image and Fit"]
    end

    subgraph "Topology & Metadata Generation"
        GenTop["generate_topology()"]
        GenMeta["generate_metadata()"]
    end

    subgraph "Outputs"
        TopFile["topology.json"]
        MetaFile["metadata.json"]
    end

    StructCorr --> GenTop
    Mapping --> GenMeta
    ImageFit --> GenTop
    GenTop --> TopFile
    GenMeta --> MetaFile
    TopFile --> "Database"
    MetaFile --> "Database"
```

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py), [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py)

## Topology Generation

### Purpose and Components

The topology file represents the molecular structure in a standardized JSON format, capturing all essential structural elements including atoms, bonds, residues, and chains. This representation serves as the foundation for analysis and visualization.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Topology {
        atom_names[]
        atom_elements[]
        atom_charges[]
        atom_residue_indices[]
        atom_bonds[][]
        residue_names[]
        residue_numbers[]
        residue_icodes{}
        residue_chain_indices[]
        chain_names[]
        residue_mappings{}
        pbc_residues[]
        cg_residues[]
    }
    
    Topology --|> Structure : derived from
```

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py:1-84](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py)

### Topology Generation Process

The topology generation process extracts structural information from the corrected structure object and organizes it into arrays and dictionaries suitable for JSON serialization:

1. **Atom Information**: Names, elements, charges, and corresponding residue indices
2. **Bond Information**: Connections between atoms, properly sorted by indices
3. **Residue Information**: Names, numbers, insertion codes, and chain indices
4. **Chain Information**: Chain names
5. **Special Residue Sets**: PBC residues, CG residues

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Structure["Structure Object"] --> AtomExtract["Extract Atom Properties"]
    AtomExtract --> AtomArrays["atom_names[]\natom_elements[]\natom_residue_indices[]"]
    
    Structure --> BondExtract["Extract Bond Information"]
    BondExtract --> BondArrays["atom_bonds[][]"]
    
    Structure --> ResidueExtract["Extract Residue Properties"]
    ResidueExtract --> ResidueArrays["residue_names[]\nresidue_numbers[]\nresidue_icodes{}\nresidue_chain_indices[]"]
    
    Structure --> ChainExtract["Extract Chain Properties"]
    ChainExtract --> ChainArrays["chain_names[]"]
    
    AtomArrays --> Topology["Topology JSON"]
    BondArrays --> Topology
    ResidueArrays --> Topology
    ChainArrays --> Topology
    
    Charges["Atom Charges"] --> Topology
    ResidueMap["Residue Mappings"] --> Topology
    PBCResidues["PBC Residues"] --> Topology
    CGResidues["CG Residues"] --> Topology
```

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py:5-84](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py)

### Handling Special Cases

The topology generation handles several special cases:

- **Missing Bonds**: If bonds cannot be determined (e.g., for coarse-grained atoms), they are represented as `float('nan')` in the JSON
- **Insertion Codes**: Stored as a dictionary with residue indices as keys, only for residues that have insertion codes
- **Missing Charges**: If charges are not available, they are set to `None` (which becomes `null` in JSON)

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py:30-31, 38-52, 61-64](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py)

## Metadata Generation

### Project Metadata

Project metadata contains comprehensive information about the molecular dynamics simulation, providing context for analysis and database queries. The metadata is organized into various categories:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ProjectMetadata {
        NAME: string
        DESCRIPTION: string
        AUTHORS: string[]
        GROUPS: string[]
        CONTACT: string
        PROGRAM: string
        VERSION: string
        TYPE: string
        METHOD: string
        LICENSE: string
        LINKCENSE: string
        CITATION: string
        THANKS: string
        LINKS: object[]
        PDBIDS: string[]
        REFERENCES: string[]
        LIGANDS: string[]
        PROTSEQ: object
        NUCLSEQ: object
        DOMAINS: object
        FRAMESTEP: number
        TIMESTEP: number
        TEMP: number
        ENSEMBLE: string
        FF: string[]
        WAT: string
        BOXTYPE: string
        SYSTATS: number
        PROTATS: number
        INTERACTIONS: object[]
        BOXSIZE_: number
        PTM: string[]
        COLLECTIONS: string[]
        WARNINGS: string[]
    }
```

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py:100-186](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py)

### Key Metadata Categories

The project metadata encompasses several key categories:

1. **Project Identification**: Name, description, authors, groups, contact information
2. **Simulation Details**: Program, version, type, method, ensemble, timestep, temperature
3. **Structure Statistics**: Atom counts, residue counts for various molecule types (protein, nucleic, lipid, etc.)
4. **Box Information**: Box type and dimensions
5. **Molecular Components**: References, ligands, protein sequences, interactions
6. **Technical Information**: Force fields, water model, post-translational modifications
7. **Special Collections**: Collection-specific fields (e.g., CV19, nanobodies)
8. **Issues**: Warning messages from the processing pipeline

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py:100-186](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py), [model_workflow/resources/inputs_file_template.yml:9-183](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/resources/inputs_file_template.yml)

### MD Simulation Metadata

For individual MD simulations within a project, a separate metadata file is generated with simulation-specific information:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class MDMetadata {
        name: string
        frames: number
        atoms: number
        refframe: number
        warnings: string[]
        metadata: object
    }
```

The `metadata` field within MD metadata may contain any of the standard metadata fields that differ from the project-level values.

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py:198-244](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py)

## Metadata Generation Process

The process of generating metadata involves collecting information from various sources:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    InputFile["inputs.yml"] --> GetInput["get_input()"]
    Structure["Structure Object"] --> AtomCount["get_atoms_count()"]
    Structure --> PTMs["structure.find_ptms()"]
    Structure --> SequenceMeta["get_sequence_metadata()"]
    
    GetInput --> MetadataGen["generate_project_metadata()"]
    AtomCount --> MetadataGen
    SequenceMeta --> MetadataGen
    PTMs --> MetadataGen
    BoxSize["get_box_size()"] --> MetadataGen
    ResidueMap["residue_map"] --> MetadataGen
    PDBIDs["pdb_ids"] --> MetadataGen
    Register["register"] --> MetadataGen
    ProcessedInteractions["processed_interactions"] --> MetadataGen
    
    MetadataGen --> MetadataJSON["metadata.json"]
```

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py:11-186](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py)

### Key Data Sources for Metadata

The metadata generation relies on several key data sources:

1. **User Inputs**: Values from the inputs.yml file, accessed through the `get_input` function
2. **Structure Analysis**: Atom counts, post-translational modifications
3. **Box Analysis**: Box dimensions from the trajectory
4. **Sequence Analysis**: Protein and nucleic acid sequences, domains
5. **Residue Mapping**: References to external databases (e.g., UniProt)
6. **Interaction Analysis**: Processed molecular interactions
7. **Register**: Warnings and errors from the processing pipeline

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py:11-186](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py), [model_workflow/resources/inputs_file_template.yml:9-519](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/resources/inputs_file_template.yml)

The topology and metadata generation steps integrate into the overall MDDB-workflow system as final processing steps before analysis:

## Key Functions

### generate_topology

The `generate_topology` function creates a JSON representation of the molecular structure:

```python
def generate_topology(
    structure: 'Structure',
    charges: List[int],
    residue_map: dict,
    pbc_residues: List[int],
    cg_residues: List[int],
    output_topology_filepath: str
)
```

Parameters:
- `structure`: The Structure object containing all molecular information
- `charges`: List of atomic charges (can be MISSING_CHARGES)
- `residue_map`: Dictionary mapping residues to external references
- `pbc_residues`: List of residue indices under periodic boundary conditions
- `cg_residues`: List of coarse-grained residue indices
- `output_topology_filepath`: Path to save the generated JSON file

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py:5-84](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py)

### generate_project_metadata

The `generate_project_metadata` function creates metadata for the entire project:

```python
def generate_project_metadata(
    input_structure_filename: str,
    input_trajectory_filename: str,
    get_input: Callable,
    structure: 'Structure',
    residue_map: dict,
    protein_references_file: 'File',
    pdb_ids: List[str],
    register: dict,
    output_metadata_filename: str,
    ligand_customized_names: str,
    processed_interactions: list
)
```

Parameters:
- `input_structure_filename`: Path to the input structure file
- `input_trajectory_filename`: Path to the input trajectory file
- `get_input`: Function to retrieve values from the inputs file
- `structure`: The Structure object
- `residue_map`: Dictionary mapping residues to external references
- `protein_references_file`: File containing protein reference information
- `pdb_ids`: List of PDB identifiers
- `register`: Register containing warnings and test results
- `output_metadata_filename`: Path to save the metadata file
- `ligand_customized_names`: Custom names for ligands
- `processed_interactions`: List of processed molecular interactions

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py:11-186](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py)

### generate_md_metadata

The `generate_md_metadata` function creates metadata for an individual MD simulation:

```python
def generate_md_metadata(
    md_inputs: dict,
    structure: 'Structure',
    snapshots: int,
    reference_frame: int,
    register: dict,
    output_metadata_filename: str
)
```

Parameters:
- `md_inputs`: Dictionary of MD-specific inputs
- `structure`: The Structure object
- `snapshots`: Number of frames in the trajectory
- `reference_frame`: Reference frame for the simulation
- `register`: Register containing warnings and test results
- `output_metadata_filename`: Path to save the metadata file

Sources: [model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py:198-244](https://github.com/mmb-irb/MDDB-workflow/blob/main/model_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py)

## Summary

The Topology and Metadata Generation components are crucial final steps in the processing pipeline of the MDDB-workflow system. They convert the processed molecular structure and simulation data into standardized JSON formats that can be easily stored in a database and accessed by analysis and visualization tools.

The topology file provides a comprehensive representation of the molecular structure, while the metadata file captures contextual information about the simulation, including parameters, statistics, and references to external databases. Together, these files enable efficient storage, retrieval, and analysis of molecular dynamics simulations in the MDDB database.

# Page: Analysis Modules

# Analysis Modules

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [model_workflow/mwf.py](model_workflow/mwf.py)
- [model_workflow/utils/constants.py](model_workflow/utils/constants.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Overview

Analysis modules in the MDDB-workflow form a comprehensive suite of tools for extracting meaningful information from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. These modules calculate various properties related to the structure, energetics, dynamics, and interactions within the simulated system. This page documents the available analysis modules, their organization, execution patterns, and how they fit into the overall workflow.

For information about the overall processing pipeline prior to analysis, see [Processing Pipeline](#3).

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:56-80]()

## Analysis Module Architecture

Analysis modules operate as standalone functions that are called from the MD class. Each module follows a consistent execution pattern that handles dependency checking, output file management, and parameter preparation.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Analysis Execution Pattern"
        Start[MD Analysis Request] --> Check{Output\nExists?}
        Check -- No --> Parameters["Prepare\nParameters"]
        Check -- Yes --> Overwrite{Overwrite\nFlag Set?}
        Overwrite -- Yes --> Parameters
        Overwrite -- No --> Return["Return\nExisting Results"]
        Parameters --> Execute["Run Analysis\nFunction"]
        Execute --> SaveResults["Save JSON\nOutput"]
        SaveResults --> Return
    end
```

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1410-1757]()

### Common Analysis Parameters

Most analysis modules share a standard set of parameters:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| input_structure_file/input_topology_file | Structure file used for topological information |
| input_trajectory_file | Trajectory file containing simulation frames |
| output_analysis_filepath | Where the analysis results are saved (JSON format) |
| structure | Structure object representation |
| snapshots | Total number of frames in the trajectory |
| frames_limit | Maximum number of frames to analyze (for performance) |
| pbc_selection | Selection of atoms in periodic boundary conditions |

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1410-1757]()

| Analysis | Output Filename |
|----------|----------------|

| RMSF | mda.fluctuation.json |
| PCA | mda.pca.json |
| Clusters | mda.clusters.json |
| SASA | mda.sasa.json |

| Membrane Thickness | mda.thickness.json |

## Structural Analyses

Structural analyses evaluate conformational changes and structural properties of the molecular system throughout the simulation.

### RMSD Analysis

Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) measures the average distance between atoms of superimposed structures, quantifying conformational changes over time.

```python
MD.run_rmsds_analysis()  # Method in MD class to execute RMSD analysis
```

The analysis calculates RMSD in several ways:
- Against the first frame
- Against the average structure
- For different selections (all atoms, backbone, etc.)
- Per-ligand RMSD where applicable

Output file: `mda.rmsds.json`

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1410-1436]()

### RMSF Analysis

Root Mean Square Fluctuation (RMSF) measures the deviation of a particle's position over time, identifying flexible and rigid regions of the molecule.

```python
MD.run_rmsf_analysis()  # Method in MD class to execute RMSF analysis
```

Output file: `mda.fluctuation.json`

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1462-1481]()

### Radius of Gyration

Radius of gyration (RGYR) measures the compactness of the molecular structure throughout the simulation.

```python
MD.run_rgyr_analysis()  # Method in MD class to execute RGYR analysis
```

Output file: `mda.rgyr.json`

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1482-1506]()

### Principal Component Analysis

Principal Component Analysis (PCA) identifies the dominant modes of motion in the simulation.

```python
MD.run_pca_analysis()  # Method in MD class to execute PCA analysis
```

This analysis also generates projection trajectory files with prefix `mdt.pca_trajectory`.

Output file: `mda.pca.json`

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1507-1534](), [model_workflow/utils/constants.py:157]()

### Clustering Analysis

Clustering groups similar conformations from the trajectory, identifying major conformational states.

```python
MD.run_clusters_analysis()  # Method in MD class to execute clustering analysis
```

This analysis generates both a JSON results file and visualization screenshots.

Output files: 
- `mda.clusters.json`
- `mdf.clusters_*_screenshot_??.jpg`

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1608-1646](), [model_workflow/utils/constants.py:148]()

## Energy Analyses

Energy analyses evaluate the energetic properties and interactions within the molecular system.

### Energy Analysis

Calculates various energy components of the system and interactions between parts of the molecule.

```python
MD.run_energies_analysis()  # Method in MD class to execute energy analysis
```

This analysis creates a directory with intermediate files before generating the final output.

Output file: `energies/mda.energies.json`

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1732-1757](), [model_workflow/utils/constants.py:178]()

### SASA Analysis

Solvent Accessible Surface Area (SASA) calculates the area of the molecule that is accessible to solvent.

```python
MD.run_sas_analysis()  # Method in MD class to execute SASA analysis
```

Output file: `mda.sasa.json`

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1708-1730]()

### Dihedral Energies

Analyzes the energy associated with dihedral angles in the molecule.

```python
MD.run_dihedral_energies()  # Method in MD class to execute dihedral energy analysis
```

Output file: `mda.dihenergies.json`

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1760-1771]()

MD.run_hbonds_analysis()  # Method in MD class to execute hydrogen bonds analysis

## Integration with Workflow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Project as Project Class
    participant MD as MD Class
    participant Analysis as Analysis Modules
    
    User->>Project: Request to run analyses
    Project->>MD: For each MD simulation
    
    loop For each analysis
        MD->>MD: Check if output exists or override flag is set
        
        alt Need to run analysis
            MD->>Analysis: Call analysis function with parameters
            Analysis->>Analysis: Process structure and trajectory data
            Analysis->>MD: Return analysis results
            MD->>MD: Save results to JSON file
        end
    end
    
    MD->>Project: Analysis complete
    Project->>User: All analyses complete
```

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1410-1757]()

## Running Analyses

Analyses can be executed through the `mwf` command-line interface or by calling the analysis methods directly on an MD object. Most analyses are executed automatically when running a full workflow, but they can also be run individually.

### Command Line Interface

```bash
# Run all default analyses
mwf run -top topology.prmtop -traj trajectory.xtc

# Run with specific analyses
mwf run -top topology.prmtop -traj trajectory.xtc -ana rmsds,rmsf,pca
```

### Programmatic Interface

```python
from model_workflow.mwf import Project, MD

# Create a project and access an MD object
project = Project(directory="./my_project")
md = project.mds[0]

# Run specific analyses
md.run_rmsds_analysis()
md.run_pca_analysis()
md.run_energies_analysis()
```

Sources: [model_workflow/mwf.py:1410-1757]()

## Summary

The analysis modules in MDDB-workflow provide a comprehensive set of tools for analyzing molecular dynamics simulations. Each module focuses on specific aspects of the simulation, from structural changes to energetic properties to specialized analyses for membranes and advanced techniques. The modules are designed to be both automatic, running as part of the standard workflow, and flexible, allowing users to select and customize the analyses they need.

## Purpose and Scope

This document details the structural analysis modules within the MDDB-workflow system. These analyses examine the conformational behavior and structural properties of molecules in molecular dynamics simulations. The analyses covered here focus on quantifying structural changes, identifying movement patterns, and characterizing structural features across trajectory frames.

For energy-related analyses, see [Energy Analyses](#4.2). For membrane-specific analyses, see [Membrane Analyses](#4.3). For more advanced analyses including pockets and helical parameters, see [Advanced Analyses](#4.4).

## Overview of Structural Analysis Modules

The MDDB-workflow provides several core structural analysis modules that work with the trajectory data processed by the pipeline. These analyses provide critical insights into the conformational dynamics of molecular systems.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Structural Analysis Modules"
        RMSD["RMSD Analysis
              (rmsds.py)"]
        RMSF["RMSF Analysis
              (rmsf.py)"]
        PCA["Principal Component Analysis
             (pca.py)"]
        RGYR["Radius of Gyration
              (rgyr.py)"]
        RMSDCheck["RMSD Trajectory Check
                  (rmsd_check.py)"]
        RMSDPer["RMSD Per Residue
                (rmsd_per_residue.py)"]
        RMSDPair["RMSD Pairwise
                 (rmsd_pairwise.py)"]
        Clusters["Cluster Analysis
                 (clusters.py)"]
        TMScores["TM Scores
                 (tmscores.py)"]
        Pockets["Pocket Analysis
                (pockets.py)"]
    end
    
    MD["MD Class"] --> RMSD & RMSF & PCA & RGYR & RMSDCheck
    MD --> RMSDPer & RMSDPair & Clusters & TMScores & Pockets
    
    Structure["Structure Class"] -.-> RMSD & RMSF & PCA & RGYR & RMSDCheck
    Structure -.-> RMSDPer & RMSDPair & Clusters & TMScores & Pockets
    
    RMSD & RMSF & PCA & RGYR & RMSDCheck & RMSDPer & RMSDPair & Clusters & TMScores & Pockets --> JSON[("Analysis JSON Files")]
```

## Core Structural Analysis Modules

### RMSD Analysis

Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) analysis calculates the average distance between atoms in different structural conformations. This analysis quantifies how much a structure deviates from a reference structure over the trajectory.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant MD as "MD Class"
    participant RMSD as "rmsds function"
    participant Gromacs as "Gromacs rms"
    participant File as "JSON Output"
    
    MD->>RMSD: Call with structure, trajectory, and selections
    Note over RMSD: Create selections for protein, nucleic acid, and ligands
    Note over RMSD: Filter out PBC (Periodic Boundary Condition) atoms
    
    loop For each reference structure (first frame, average)
        loop For each selection (protein, nucleic, ligands)
            RMSD->>Gromacs: Run RMSD calculation
            Gromacs-->>RMSD: Return XVG data
            RMSD->>RMSD: Parse XVG and convert to Ångstroms
        end
    end
    
    RMSD->>File: Save RMSD values with metadata
    File-->>MD: Return success
```

The RMSD analysis module (`rmsds.py`) performs the following key functions:

1. Calculates RMSD for different reference structures:
   - First frame of the trajectory
   - Average structure

2. Analyzes different structural components separately:
   - Protein
   - Nucleic acid
   - Ligands (if present)

3. Handles periodic boundary conditions (PBC) by excluding PBC atoms from the analysis

4. Creates a reduced trajectory if the original trajectory exceeds the frame limit

The output is saved as a JSON file containing RMSD values for each selection and reference structure.

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/rmsds.py:10-118]()

### RMSF Analysis

Root Mean Square Fluctuation (RMSF) measures the average deviation of atom positions from their mean position over the trajectory. This analysis helps identify flexible and rigid regions of a molecule.

The RMSF module (`rmsf.py`) performs the following:

1. Uses MDAnalysis to calculate RMSF values for all atoms
2. Filters out values from PBC residue atoms as they may not have meaningful fluctuations
3. Computes statistical properties (mean, standard deviation, min, max) of the RMSF values
4. Outputs a JSON file with RMSF data for each atom and summary statistics

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Trajectory &\nTopology"]-->MDAnalysis["MDAnalysis Universe"]
    MDAnalysis-->RMSFCalculation["RMSF Calculation\n(rms.RMSF)"]
    RMSFCalculation-->Filtering["Filter PBC Atoms"]
    Filtering-->Statistics["Calculate Statistics\n(mean, stddev, min, max)"]
    Statistics-->Output["JSON Output"]
```

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/rmsf.py:1-64]()

### Trajectory Integrity Check

The trajectory integrity check (`rmsd_check.py`) ensures that the trajectory doesn't contain any unphysical jumps or discontinuities. This is an important quality control step that:

1. Calculates frame-to-frame RMSD to detect sudden jumps
2. Uses statistical analysis to identify outliers in the RMSD pattern
3. Can analyze the trajectory as a whole or by fragments
4. Provides flexibility through the "mercy" parameter for handling problematic trajectories

The check works by:
1. Loading the trajectory frame by frame
2. Computing RMSD between consecutive frames
3. Detecting outliers using z-score analysis
4. Failing the test if any outliers are detected (unless mercy is granted)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Trajectory &\nStructure"]-->LoadTraj["Load Trajectory"]
    LoadTraj-->ParseSelection["Parse Check Selection\nRemove PBC Atoms"]
    
    ParseSelection-->EmptyCheck{"Selection\nEmpty?"}
    EmptyCheck-->|Yes|SkipTest["Skip Test\n(NA)"]
    EmptyCheck-->|No|FrameLoop["Iterate Through Frames"]
    
    FrameLoop-->CalculateRMSD["Calculate RMSD Between\nConsecutive Frames"]
    CalculateRMSD-->ComputeStats["Compute Mean and StdDev"]
    ComputeStats-->IdentifyOutliers["Identify Outliers\n(Z-score > cutoff)"]
    
    IdentifyOutliers-->OutliersCheck{"Found\nOutliers?"}
    OutliersCheck-->|Yes|MercyCheck{"In Mercy\nList?"}
    MercyCheck-->|Yes|Warning["Add Warning\nPass with Warning"]
    MercyCheck-->|No|Failure["Test Failure"]
    OutliersCheck-->|No|Success["Test Passed"]
```

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/rmsd_check.py:12-145]()

### Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

Principal Component Analysis (PCA) identifies the most significant motions in a molecular dynamics trajectory by reducing the dimensionality of the data. The PCA module (`pca.py`) performs the following:

1. Prepares a reduced trajectory if needed
2. Superimposes all frames on a reference (first frame)
3. Performs PCA using scikit-learn on atom coordinates
4. Generates trajectory projections along principal components
5. Saves eigenvalues, projections, and atom indices to a JSON file

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Trajectory &\nStructure"] --> GetReduced["Get Reduced Trajectory"]
    GetReduced --> SelectAtoms["Select Atoms for Analysis\n(Remove PBC Atoms)"]
    SelectAtoms --> LoadTrajectory["Load Trajectory"]
    LoadTrajectory --> SuperimposeFrames["Superimpose Frames"]
    SuperimposeFrames --> ReshapeData["Reshape for PCA"]
    ReshapeData --> PerformPCA["Perform PCA\n(sklearn.decomposition.PCA)"]
    PerformPCA --> ExtractResults["Extract Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors"]
    ExtractResults --> GenerateProjections["Generate Trajectory Projections"]
    GenerateProjections --> SaveOutput["Save Output JSON"]
```

The PCA analysis provides insight into:
- Major collective motions of the system
- The relative importance of each motion (eigenvalues)
- The direction and magnitude of atomic movements (eigenvectors)
- Conformational changes along the most significant modes

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/pca.py:1-137]()

### RMSD Per Residue

The RMSD per residue analysis (`rmsd_per_residue.py`) calculates RMSD values for each residue individually, providing insight into which parts of a molecule show the most significant structural changes.

Key features of this module:
1. Uses PyTraj to calculate RMSD for each residue
2. Handles reduction of trajectory frames if needed
3. Filters out PBC atoms which may have boundary-crossing artifacts
4. Maps PyTraj residue indices back to the original structure indices
5. Creates a comprehensive residue-by-residue RMSD profile

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Trajectory &\nStructure"] --> GetReduced["Get Reduced Trajectory"]
    GetReduced --> FilterPBC["Filter PBC Atoms"]
    FilterPBC --> PyTraj["PyTraj Analysis\n(rmsd_perres)"]
    PyTraj --> MapIndices["Map Residue Indices"]
    MapIndices --> SaveJSON["Save JSON Output"]
```

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/rmsd_per_residue.py:1-89]()

### RMSD Pairwise Analysis

The RMSD pairwise analysis (`rmsd_pairwise.py`) calculates RMSD between all pairs of frames in the trajectory, creating a matrix of structural similarities.

Key features:
1. Can analyze the overall structure and specific interactions
2. Selects representative atoms (CA for proteins, C5' for nucleic acids)
3. Filters out PBC atoms
4. Creates a comprehensive RMSD matrix
5. Outputs JSON format for easy visualization and further analysis

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/rmsd_pairwise.py:1-107]()

### Radius of Gyration (RGYR)

The radius of gyration analysis (`rgyr.py`) measures the compactness of a structure over time. It calculates the root mean square distance of atoms from their center of mass.

Key features:
1. Uses Gromacs to calculate overall RGYR and components along x, y, and z axes
2. Creates a reduced trajectory if needed
3. Filters out PBC atoms
4. Calculates statistical properties (mean, standard deviation, min, max)
5. Outputs both time series and summary statistics

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Trajectory &\nStructure"] --> GetReduced["Get Reduced Trajectory"]
    GetReduced --> FilterPBC["Create Non-PBC Selection"]
    FilterPBC --> RunGromacs["Run Gromacs gyrate"]
    RunGromacs --> ParseXVG["Parse XVG Output"]
    ParseXVG --> CalcStats["Calculate Statistics"]
    CalcStats --> SaveJSON["Save JSON Output"]
```

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/rgyr.py:1-121]()

## Advanced Structural Analyses

### Cluster Analysis

The cluster analysis module (`clusters.py`) identifies conformational states by grouping similar frames together based on RMSD distances.

Key features of the clustering module:
1. Performs clustering for the overall structure and individual interactions
2. Uses RMSD as a distance metric between frames
3. Automatically adjusts the RMSD cutoff to achieve a target number of clusters
4. Identifies transitions between clusters
5. Generates representative screenshots for each cluster
6. Outputs cluster members, representative frames, and transitions

The clustering algorithm works by:
1. Building a pairwise RMSD matrix between all frames
2. Setting an initial RMSD cutoff
3. Adjusting the cutoff until the desired number of clusters is achieved
4. Identifying the most representative frame for each cluster
5. Analyzing transitions between clusters

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Trajectory &\nStructure"] --> GetReduced["Get Reduced Trajectory"]
    GetReduced --> SetupSelections["Set Up Analysis Selections\n- Overall\n- Per Interaction"]
    SetupSelections --> CalculateRMSD["Calculate RMSD Matrix"]
    CalculateRMSD --> FindCutoff["Find Optimal RMSD Cutoff"]
    
    FindCutoff --> ApplyCutoff["Apply Cutoff to Find Clusters"]
    ApplyCutoff --> EnoughClusters{"Target Number\nof Clusters?"}
    EnoughClusters -->|No| AdjustCutoff["Adjust Cutoff"]
    AdjustCutoff --> ApplyCutoff
    
    EnoughClusters -->|Yes| FindRepresentative["Find Representative\nFrame for Each Cluster"]
    FindRepresentative --> AnalyzeTransitions["Analyze Cluster Transitions"]
    FindRepresentative --> TakeScreenshots["Take Screenshots"]
    
    AnalyzeTransitions & TakeScreenshots --> SaveOutput["Save Output JSON"]
```

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/clusters.py:1-273]()

### Pocket Analysis

The pocket analysis module (`pockets.py`) identifies and characterizes potential binding sites (pockets) in protein structures. This module is particularly useful for drug discovery applications.

Key features of the pocket analysis:
1. Uses the Fpocket algorithm through the MDpocket interface
2. Analyzes pockets over the trajectory to identify stable binding sites
3. Calculates the volume of each pocket over time
4. Identifies atoms lining each pocket
5. Creates a reduced trajectory for analysis (100 frames)

The pocket detection workflow:
1. Creates a grid representing pocket frequency across the trajectory
2. Identifies the most stable pockets based on frequency grid
3. Analyzes each selected pocket individually to track its dynamics
4. Calculates volumetric and other properties for each pocket

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Trajectory &\nStructure"] --> GetReduced["Get Reduced Trajectory\n(100 frames)"]
    GetReduced --> RunMDpocket["Run MDpocket\nto Find Pockets"]
    RunMDpocket --> ParseGrid["Parse Grid File"]
    ParseGrid --> IdentifyPockets["Identify Individual Pockets"]
    
    IdentifyPockets --> AnalyzePockets["Analyze Each Pocket"]
    AnalyzePockets --> ExtractVolumes["Extract Pocket Volumes"]
    AnalyzePockets --> IdentifyAtoms["Identify Atoms\nLining Each Pocket"]
    
    ExtractVolumes & IdentifyAtoms --> SaveOutput["Save Output JSON"]
```

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/pockets.py:1-527]()

### TM-Score Analysis

The TM-Score analysis module (`tmscores.py`) calculates the Template-Modeling score, which measures the similarity between protein structures. Unlike RMSD, TM-Score is less sensitive to local variations.

Key features:
1. Computes TM-Score against different reference structures
2. Focuses on Cα atoms for comparison
3. Handles PBC atoms appropriately
4. Outputs time series of TM-Score values

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/tmscores.py:1-138]()

### Markov State Analysis

The Markov state analysis module (`markov.py`) creates a simplified representation of the conformational landscape using the most populated states and the transitions between them.

Key features:
1. Identifies the most populated frames
2. Calculates RMSD between these representative frames
3. Generates screenshots for visualization
4. Creates a network representation of conformational dynamics

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Trajectory &\nPopulations"] --> SelectFrames["Select Most Populated Frames"]
    SelectFrames --> LoadFrames["Load Selected Frames"]
    LoadFrames --> CalculateRMSD["Calculate RMSD Matrix"]
    LoadFrames --> GenerateScreenshots["Generate Screenshots"]
    CalculateRMSD & GenerateScreenshots --> SaveOutput["Save Output JSON"]
```

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/markov.py:1-105]()

## Common Implementation Patterns

### Trajectory Handling

Most structural analyses follow common patterns for handling trajectories:

1. **Trajectory Reduction**: For computational efficiency, many analyses create a reduced trajectory when the original exceeds a frame limit.

```python
reduced_trajectory_filepath, step, frames = get_reduced_trajectory(
    input_topology_file,
    input_trajectory_file,
    snapshots,
    frames_limit,
)
```

2. **PBC Handling**: Periodic boundary condition atoms are typically excluded from analyses to avoid artifacts:

```python
selection -= pbc_selection
if not selection:
    print('No selection to analyze after PBC subtraction')
    return
```

3. **Tool Interfaces**: Analyses use various backends including:
   - Gromacs (via subprocess calls)
   - PyTraj
   - MDTraj
   - MDAnalysis
   - Custom Python implementations

### Output Format

All structural analyses output JSON files with a consistent structure:

```
{
  "data": [...],      # Main analysis data
  "start": 0,         # Starting frame (usually 0)
  "step": 10,         # Step between frames
  (optional fields specific to each analysis)
}
```

The consistent output format facilitates integration with visualization tools and the MDDB database.

## Integration with MD Class

The structural analysis modules are invoked by the MD class, which:

1. Prepares the necessary input files
2. Provides the Structure object
3. Handles the PBC selection
4. Manages the output file paths

This integration ensures consistent analysis workflows and proper data management.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant MD as "MD Class"
    participant Structure as "Structure Class"
    participant Analysis as "Analysis Module"
    participant Output as "JSON Output"
    
    User->>MD: Run analysis
    MD->>Structure: Get atom selections
    Structure-->>MD: Return selections
    MD->>Analysis: Call with parameters
    Analysis->>Structure: Get atom data
    Structure-->>Analysis: Return atom data
    Analysis->>Output: Save results
    Output-->>MD: Confirm completion
    MD-->>User: Return success
```

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/rmsds.py]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/rmsf.py]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/pca.py]()
- [model_workflow/tools/get_reduced_trajectory.py:32-97]()
- [model_workflow/utils/register.py:14-152]()

# Page: Energy Analyses

# Energy Analyses

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [model_workflow/analyses/energies.py](model_workflow/analyses/energies.py)
- [model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py](model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The Energy Analyses module provides tools for calculating and analyzing energetic properties of molecular dynamics simulations. This module specifically focuses on:

1. Interaction energies between molecular components (electrostatic and Van der Waals)
2. Solvent Accessible Surface Area (SASA) calculations

These analyses help researchers understand binding affinities, molecular interactions, and conformational stability within the simulated systems. For other types of analyses such as structural analyses (RMSD, RMSF), see [Structural Analyses](#4.1) or for membrane-specific analyses, see [Membrane Analyses](#4.3).

## Overview of Energy Analysis Components

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MD["MD Class"] --> |calls| Energies["energies()"]
    MD --> |calls| SASA["sasa()"]
    
    Energies --> CMIP["CMIP Tool"]
    CMIP --> |calculates| ElecEn["Electrostatic Energy"]
    CMIP --> |calculates| VdwEn["Van der Waals Energy"]
    
    SASA --> Gromacs["GROMACS sasa"]
    Gromacs --> |calculates| SASAValues["Surface Area Values"]
    
    Energies --> |produces| EnergyJSON["energy_*.json"]
    SASA --> |produces| SASAJSON["sasa.json"]
    
    subgraph "Data Processing"
        Preparation["Structure Preparation"]
        GridCalc["Grid Calculation"]
        EnergyComp["Energy Computation"]
        FrameProc["Frame Processing"]
        DataFormat["Data Formatting"]
    end
    
    Energies --> Preparation
    Preparation --> GridCalc
    GridCalc --> EnergyComp
    EnergyComp --> FrameProc
    FrameProc --> DataFormat
    DataFormat --> EnergyJSON
```

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:49-573]()
[model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py:16-152]()

## Interaction Energies Analysis

The interaction energies analysis calculates electrostatic and Van der Waals potentials between defined interaction agents in the molecular system. This is performed by the `energies()` function which leverages the CMIP (Classical Molecular Interaction Potential) tool.

### Theoretical Background

The interaction energies analysis is based on:

- **CMIP (Classical Molecular Interaction Potential)**: Calculates electrostatic and Van der Waals interaction energies between molecular components
- **ACPYPE**: A Python tool that uses Antechamber to generate topologies for chemical compounds

Key references:
- SOUSA DA SILVA, A. W. & VRANKEN, W. F. ACPYPE - AnteChamber PYthon Parser interfacE. BMC Research Notes 5 (2012)
- Gelpí, J.L., et al. Classical molecular interaction potentials: Improved setup procedure in molecular dynamics simulations of proteins. Proteins, 45: 428-437 (2001)

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:1-16]()

### Energies Analysis Workflow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant MD as MD Class
    participant Energy as energies() function
    participant CMIP as CMIP Tool
    
    MD->>Energy: Call with interactions<br>data and structure
    Note over Energy: Prepare structure<br>for CMIP
    Energy->>Energy: name_terminal_residues()
    Energy->>Energy: set_cmip_elements()
    
    loop For each interaction pair
        Note over Energy: Skip if exceeding<br>atom limit (80,000)
        Energy->>Energy: Extract frames from trajectory
        
        loop For each trajectory frame
            Energy->>Energy: pdb2cmip() for agent1 as host
            Energy->>Energy: pdb2cmip() for agent2 as host
            Energy->>Energy: pdb2cmip() for agent1 as guest
            Energy->>Energy: pdb2cmip() for agent2 as guest
            Energy->>Energy: adapt_cmip_grid()
            Energy->>CMIP: Calculate agent1 as guest energies
            Energy->>CMIP: Calculate agent2 as guest energies
            Energy->>Energy: Store frame energies
        end
        
        Energy->>Energy: Format energy data
        Energy->>Energy: Calculate average energies
        Energy->>MD: Return JSON output
    end
```

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:49-573]()

### Implementation Details

The energy analysis function handles several complex tasks:

1. **Structure Preparation**:
   - Renames terminal residues according to CMIP requirements
   - Sets element types to be CMIP-compatible (e.g., hydrogen atoms bonded to oxygen are renamed as 'HO')

2. **Interaction Processing**:
   - For each defined interaction between two molecular components:
     - Prepares special PDB files for both agents with proper charges
     - Marks atoms at the interface as "dummy" atoms when appropriate
     - Handles covalent bonds between interacting components

3. **CMIP Grid Calculation**:
   - Calculates appropriate grid dimensions to encompass both interacting components
   - Ensures grid size doesn't exceed memory limits (65 million grid points)
   - Adjusts grid resolution if necessary

4. **Energy Calculation**:
   - Runs CMIP twice for each interaction pair (each agent as guest/host)
   - Extracts Van der Waals and electrostatic energies
   - Filters extremely high energy values (>100) which might represent computational artifacts

5. **Results Processing**:
   - Averages energies across all trajectory frames
   - Separately calculates averages for first and last 20% of frames
   - Outputs per-atom energy values for all calculation types

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:141-504]()
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:581-764]()

### Key Functions and Parameters

| Function | Purpose | Key Parameters |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| `energies()` | Main function that orchestrates energy calculation | `input_trajectory_file`, `structure`, `interactions`, `charges` |
| `pdb2cmip()` | Transforms structure to CMIP-compatible format | `host_file`, `host_selection`, `guest_selection` |
| `adapt_cmip_grid()` | Calculates optimal grid dimensions | `agent1_cmip_pdb`, `agent2_cmip_pdb` |
| `get_cmip_energies()` | Executes CMIP and extracts energy values | `cmip_inputs`, `guest`, `host` |
| `format_data()` | Processes raw energy data into final format | `data` (list of energy values) |

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:49-764]()

### Output Format

The energies analysis produces JSON output with the following structure:

```
{
  "name": "interaction_name",
  "agent1": {
    "vdw": [atom1_vdw_avg, atom2_vdw_avg, ...],
    "es": [atom1_es_avg, atom2_es_avg, ...],
    "both": [atom1_both_avg, atom2_both_avg, ...],
    "ivdw": [atom1_initial_vdw_avg, ...],     // First 20% of frames
    "ies": [atom1_initial_es_avg, ...],       // First 20% of frames
    "iboth": [atom1_initial_both_avg, ...],   // First 20% of frames
    "fvdw": [atom1_final_vdw_avg, ...],       // Last 20% of frames
    "fes": [atom1_final_es_avg, ...],         // Last 20% of frames
    "fboth": [atom1_final_both_avg, ...]      // Last 20% of frames
  },
  "agent2": {
    // Same structure as agent1
  },
  "version": "1.0.0"
}
```

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:563-568]()
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:752-762]()

## Solvent Accessible Surface Area (SASA) Analysis

The SASA analysis calculates the surface area of each residue that is accessible to solvent molecules. This is implemented in the `sasa()` function which uses GROMACS to perform the calculations.

### SASA Analysis Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MD["MD Class"] --> |calls| SASA["sasa() function"]
    
    SASA --> FilterH["Filter out hydrogens"]
    FilterH --> CreateNDX["Create index file<br>for selection"]
    CreateNDX --> ExtractFrames["Extract frames<br>from trajectory"]
    
    subgraph "Frame Processing"
        RunGromacs["Run GROMACS sasa"]
        ParseXVG["Parse XVG output"]
        CalculateResidueAreas["Calculate per-residue<br>surface areas"]
        NormalizeValues["Normalize by<br>atom count"]
    end
    
    ExtractFrames --> RunGromacs
    RunGromacs --> ParseXVG
    ParseXVG --> CalculateResidueAreas
    CalculateResidueAreas --> NormalizeValues
    
    NormalizeValues --> FormatData["Format data<br>Calculate means & stddevs"]
    FormatData --> SaveJSON["Save to JSON"]
    
    PBC["PBC residues"] --> |excluded from| CalculateResidueAreas
```

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py:16-152]()

### Implementation Details

The SASA analysis performs the following steps:

1. **Preparation**:
   - Filters out hydrogen atoms from the structure for analysis
   - Creates an NDX index file for atom selection

2. **Frame Processing**:
   - Extracts frames from the trajectory
   - For each frame, runs GROMACS `sasa` command to calculate atomic surface areas
   - Parses the resulting XVG file to extract surface area values

3. **Data Processing**:
   - Aggregates atomic values to calculate per-residue surface areas
   - Excludes residues in periodic boundary conditions (PBC), such as membrane components
   - Normalizes SASA values by dividing by the number of atoms in each residue
   - Converts units from nm² to Å²

4. **Result Generation**:
   - Calculates mean and standard deviation of SASA values for each residue
   - Organizes data for JSON output

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py:34-149]()

### Key Functions and Parameters

| Function | Purpose | Key Parameters |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| `sasa()` | Main function for SASA calculation | `input_topology_filename`, `input_trajectory_filename`, `structure`, `pbc_residues` |
| `xvg_parse()` | Parses GROMACS XVG output files | Called internally with output from GROMACS |
| `get_pdb_frames()` | Extracts frames from trajectory | `input_topology_filename`, `input_trajectory_filename`, `snapshots`, `frames_limit` |

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py:16-23]()

### Output Format

The SASA analysis produces JSON output with the following structure:

```
{
  "step": frame_step_size,
  "saspf": [
    [residue1_frame1_sasa, residue1_frame2_sasa, ...],
    [residue2_frame1_sasa, residue2_frame2_sasa, ...],
    ...
  ],
  "means": [residue1_mean, residue2_mean, ...],
  "stdvs": [residue1_stddev, residue2_stddev, ...]
}
```

Note: For residues in periodic boundary conditions (PBC), the corresponding values in the arrays are set to `null`.

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py:144-149]()

## Integration with MD Class

Energy analyses are integrated into the broader MDDB-workflow through the MD class, which manages the execution of these analyses as part of the overall processing pipeline.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Project as Project Class
    participant MD as MD Class
    participant Energy as Energy Analyses
    
    User->>Project: Create project
    Project->>MD: Create MD instance
    
    MD->>MD: Process inputs
    MD->>MD: Process structure
    MD->>MD: Process interactions
    MD->>MD: Generate metadata
    
    Note over MD,Energy: Energy analyses occur<br>after core processing
    
    MD->>Energy: Call energies()<br>with interactions data
    Energy-->>MD: Return energy results
    
    MD->>Energy: Call sasa()<br>with structure data
    Energy-->>MD: Return SASA results
    
    MD->>MD: Save analysis results<br>as JSON files
    MD-->>Project: Report completion
    Project-->>User: Return status
```

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:49-573]()
[model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py:16-152]()

## Limitations and Considerations

When using the energy analyses, keep in mind the following limitations:

1. **Atom Count Limits**:
   - CMIP has a hard limit of 80,000 atoms per interacting agent
   - Interactions exceeding this limit are skipped with a warning

2. **Grid Size Management**:
   - Grid points are limited to 65 million to prevent memory errors
   - When exceeded, grid resolution is automatically reduced

3. **SASA Considerations**:
   - PBC residues (e.g., membrane components) are excluded from results
   - SASA values are normalized by atom count for better comparability

4. **Computational Requirements**:
   - Energy analyses are computationally intensive
   - Backup files are created during processing to allow resuming if interrupted

Sources:
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:101-112]()
[model_workflow/analyses/energies.py:282-299]()
[model_workflow/analyses/sasa.py:29-32]()

# Membrane Analyses

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

## Overview

The Membrane Analyses module provides specialized tools for analyzing structural and dynamic properties of lipid membranes in molecular dynamics simulations. This set of tools identifies membrane structures within simulations and performs various analyses to characterize their properties, including thickness, lipid order parameters, area per lipid, density distributions, and lipid-protein interactions.

The membrane analyses are performed following the mapping and identification of membrane components, which is a prerequisite step that automatically detects lipid molecules in the system based on their InChI keys.

Sources:
- [model_workflow/tools/generate_membrane_mapping.py:13-169]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/thickness.py:9-65]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/lipid_order.py:9-169]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py:11-76]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/density.py:7-67]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/lipid_interactions.py:9-56]()

## Membrane Identification Pipeline

Before any membrane analysis can be performed, the system needs to identify which molecules constitute membranes in the simulation. This is accomplished through the membrane mapping process.

### Membrane Mapping Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Structure["Structure"] --> InChIKeys["Get InChI Keys"]
    InChIKeys --> LipidID["Lipid Identification<br>via SwissLipids & LIPID_MAPS"]
    LipidID --> PolarAtoms["Extract Polar Atoms<br>from Lipids"]
    PolarAtoms --> FATSLiM["Run FATSLiM<br>for Membrane Detection"]
    FATSLiM --> MemMap["Membrane Mapping<br>- Number of membranes<br>- Leaflet assignment<br>- Polar atom groups"]

    classDef process fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class Structure,InChIKeys,LipidID,PolarAtoms,FATSLiM,MemMap process;
```

The membrane mapping process:

1. **InChI Key Generation**: Extracts InChI keys for non-protein, non-nucleic acid residues in the structure.
2. **Lipid Identification**: Queries external databases (SwissLipids and LIPID_MAPS) to identify lipid molecules.
3. **Polar Atom Selection**: Identifies polar atoms within lipids for membrane detection.
4. **Membrane Detection**: Uses FATSLiM to identify membranes and assign atoms to upper or lower leaflets.
5. **Mapping Generation**: Creates a comprehensive mapping of membrane components for subsequent analyses.

Sources:
- [model_workflow/tools/generate_membrane_mapping.py:13-169]()
- [model_workflow/tools/get_inchi_keys.py:72-169]()

### Membrane Data Structure

The membrane mapping generates a structured data object containing information about all identified membranes:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class MembraneMapping {
        n_mems: int
        mems: Dict
        no_mem_lipid: List
        references: Dict
    }
    
    class Membrane {
        leaflets: Dict
        polar_atoms: Dict
    }
    
    class Leaflet {
        bot: List[int]
        top: List[int]
    }
    
    class PolarAtoms {
        bot: List[int]
        top: List[int]
    }
    
    class References {
        inchikey: Dict
    }
    
    class MoleculeReference {
        resname: str
        resindices: List[int]
        indices: List[int]
        swisslipids: Dict
        lipidmaps: Dict
    }
    
    MembraneMapping "1" --> "*" Membrane: mems
    MembraneMapping "1" --> "1" References: references
    Membrane "1" --> "1" Leaflet: leaflets
    Membrane "1" --> "1" PolarAtoms: polar_atoms
    References "1" --> "*" MoleculeReference: inchikey
```

The membrane mapping is stored as a JSON object with the following structure:
- `n_mems`: Number of membranes identified
- `mems`: Dictionary of membrane objects, each containing:
  - `leaflets`: Dictionary with `bot` and `top` lists of atom indices
  - `polar_atoms`: Dictionary with `bot` and `top` lists of polar atom indices
- `no_mem_lipid`: List of atom indices belonging to lipids not assigned to a membrane
- `references`: Dictionary mapping InChI keys to lipid molecule information

Sources:
- [model_workflow/tools/generate_membrane_mapping.py:47-162]()

## Membrane Structural Analyses

The system provides several analyses for characterizing membrane structural properties.

### Membrane Thickness Analysis

The thickness analysis calculates the distance between leaflets of a membrane, providing insights into membrane structure and fluidity.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    TrajFile["Trajectory File"] --> ZPos["lpp_zpositions<br>(BioBB LiPyphilic)"]
    StructFile["Structure File"] --> ZPos
    MemMap["Membrane Mapping"] --> HeadSel["Extract Headgroup<br>Selections"]
    HeadSel --> ZPos
    ZPos --> CSVFile[".zpositions.csv"]
    CSVFile --> Process["Process Results"]
    TrajFile --> MidplaneCalc["Calculate Midplane Z<br>using PyTraj"]
    Process --> ThicknessData["Thickness Data<br>- mean_positive<br>- mean_negative<br>- thickness<br>- std_thickness"]
    MidplaneCalc --> ThicknessData
```

The thickness analysis:
1. Selects polar headgroup atoms from the membrane mapping
2. Uses BioBB LiPyphilic's ZPositions module to calculate leaflet positions
3. Calculates the midplane Z-position using PyTraj
4. Computes membrane thickness and associated statistics

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/thickness.py:9-65]()

### Area per Lipid Analysis

The area per lipid (APL) analysis calculates the surface area occupied by each lipid molecule in the membrane, a key parameter for membrane fluidity and phase behavior.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    TrajFile["Trajectory File"] --> APL["fatslim_apl<br>(BioBB FATSLiM)"]
    StructFile["Structure File"] --> APL
    MemMap["Membrane Mapping"] --> HeadSel["Extract Headgroup<br>Selections"]
    HeadSel --> APL
    APL --> CSVFile[".apl.csv"]
    CSVFile --> Process["process_apl<br>- Create 2D grids<br>- Calculate statistics"]
    Process --> APLData["APL Data<br>- lower leaflet grid<br>- upper leaflet grid<br>- median<br>- std"]
```

The area per lipid analysis:
1. Selects polar headgroup atoms from the membrane mapping
2. Uses BioBB FATSLiM's APL module to calculate area per lipid
3. Processes results to create 2D grids for each leaflet
4. Computes median and standard deviation of area per lipid values

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py:11-76]()

### Lipid Order Parameter Analysis

The lipid order parameter analysis calculates the orientational order of lipid acyl chains, providing insights into membrane packing and phase.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    TrajFile["Trajectory File"] --> MDAnalysis["MDAnalysis<br>Universe"]
    Topology["Topology File"] --> MDAnalysis
    MemMap["Membrane Mapping"] --> References["Process Lipid<br>References"]
    References --> ChainID["Identify Acyl Chains<br>& C-H Bonds"]
    MDAnalysis --> ChainID
    ChainID --> OrderCalc["Calculate Order<br>Parameters<br>S = 0.5*(3*〈cos²θ〉 - 1)"]
    MDAnalysis --> OrderCalc
    OrderCalc --> OrderData["Order Parameter Data<br>- Per carbon atom<br>- Per acyl chain<br>- Per lipid type"]
```

The lipid order parameter analysis:
1. Processes lipid references from the membrane mapping
2. Identifies acyl chains and C-H bonds in lipid molecules
3. Special handling for cholesterol vs. non-cholesterol lipids
4. Calculates order parameters S = 0.5*(3*〈cos²θ〉 - 1), where θ is the angle between C-H bonds and membrane normal
5. Computes averages and standard deviations for each lipid carbon atom

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/lipid_order.py:9-169]()

## Membrane Component Analyses

### Density Distribution Analysis

The density analysis calculates various density distributions (number, mass, charge, electron) along the membrane normal (z-axis).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    TrajFile["Trajectory File"] --> PyTraj["PyTraj<br>Trajectory Iterator"]
    StructFile["Structure File"] --> PyTraj
    Structure["Structure Object"] --> ComponentSel["Component Selections<br>- Per chain<br>- Polar atoms"]
    MemMap["Membrane Mapping"] --> PolarSel["Extract Polar<br>Atom Selections"]
    PolarSel --> ComponentSel
    ComponentSel --> DensityCalc["Calculate Density<br>- number<br>- mass<br>- charge<br>- electron"]
    PyTraj --> DensityCalc
    DensityCalc --> DensityData["Density Distribution Data<br>- Z-positions<br>- Component densities<br>- Standard deviations"]
```

The density distribution analysis:
1. Creates selections for each chain and for polar atoms from the membrane mapping
2. Uses PyTraj to calculate various density distributions along the z-axis
3. Processes results for each component and density type
4. Compiles density profiles and associated statistics

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/density.py:7-67]()

### Lipid-Protein Interactions Analysis

The lipid-protein interactions analysis identifies and quantifies which lipids interact with which protein residues.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    TrajFile["Trajectory File"] --> MDAnalysis["MDAnalysis<br>Universe"]
    Topology["Topology File"] --> MDAnalysis
    MemMap["Membrane Mapping"] --> LipidNames["Extract Lipid<br>Residue Names"]
    MDAnalysis --> ProteinRes["Select Protein<br>Residues"]
    LipidNames --> Selection["Selection:<br>(around 6 protein) and<br>(resname LIPIDS) and<br>not protein"]
    ProteinRes --> ResInteractions["For Each Residue:<br>Find Nearby Lipids"]
    Selection --> ResInteractions
    MDAnalysis --> ResInteractions
    ResInteractions --> OccupancyCalc["Calculate Occupancy<br>(normalized counts)"]
    OccupancyCalc --> InteractionData["Lipid-Protein<br>Interaction Data<br>- Per protein residue<br>- Per lipid type"]
```

The lipid-protein interactions analysis:
1. Extracts lipid names from the membrane mapping
2. Identifies protein residues in the system
3. For each trajectory frame, finds lipids within 6Å of each protein residue
4. Counts and normalizes occurrences to calculate lipid occupancy around protein residues

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/lipid_interactions.py:9-56]()

## Integration in the Analysis Pipeline

The membrane analyses are integrated into the overall MDDB workflow analysis pipeline, where they are executed after metadata generation if a membrane is detected in the system.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MD["MD Class"] --> CheckMembrane{"Membrane<br>Detected?"}
    CheckMembrane -->|No| Skip["Skip Membrane<br>Analyses"]
    CheckMembrane -->|Yes| Thickness["Membrane Thickness<br>Analysis"]
    Thickness --> APL["Area per Lipid<br>Analysis"]
    APL --> LipidOrder["Lipid Order<br>Analysis"]
    LipidOrder --> Density["Density Distribution<br>Analysis"]
    Density --> LipidInteractions["Lipid-Protein<br>Interactions Analysis"]
    LipidInteractions --> SaveResults["Save Analysis<br>Results as JSON"]
```

Each membrane analysis module follows a similar pattern:
1. Check if a membrane mapping exists and contains at least one membrane
2. Skip the analysis if no membrane is found
3. Run the specific analysis using the appropriate tools
4. Process and save the results as a JSON file

Sources:
- [model_workflow/analyses/thickness.py:17-21]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py:17-21]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/lipid_order.py:28-32]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/density.py:17-21]()
- [model_workflow/analyses/lipid_interactions.py:19-23]()

## Summary of Membrane Analysis Tools

The following table summarizes the membrane analysis modules provided by the MDDB-workflow system:

| Analysis | Purpose | External Dependencies | Output Data |
|---------|---------|---------------------|------------|
| Membrane Mapping | Identify membranes in the system | FATSLiM, SwissLipids DB, LIPID_MAPS DB | Membrane leaflets, polar atoms, lipid references |
| Thickness | Calculate membrane thickness | BioBB LiPyphilic | Mean positions, thickness, standard deviations |
| Area per Lipid | Calculate area per lipid | BioBB FATSLiM | 2D grids for each leaflet, median, standard deviation |
| Lipid Order | Calculate lipid tail ordering | MDAnalysis | Order parameters per carbon atom and acyl chain |
| Density | Calculate density distributions | PyTraj | Z-axis profiles for number, mass, charge, electron densities |
| Lipid Interactions | Analyze lipid-protein contacts | MDAnalysis | Occupancy of lipids around protein residues |

Each analysis provides insights into different aspects of membrane structure and dynamics, contributing to a comprehensive characterization of membrane systems in molecular dynamics simulations.
